lines.trans: Please go wait downstairs first—there is something I need to talk over with Ms. Cindy.
What is it you wanted to say? Go ahead.
About your guest earlier—seeing you lacked each other's numbers, she did not seem like a real best friend.
I suspect your agency arranged her appearance for the camera.
And so what?
Even if television can hardly be one hundred percent truthful, I do not think we can broadcast an outright lie.
Are you starting that lecture again? It is not as if I told a lie!
It is not that we are not friends—we are simply less close! Are all friends supposed to be super close?
Because you acted the part so convincingly, anyone watching who did not know would think the two of you were truly close.
What is it that you are actually trying to tell me?

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아니, 핑크가 어려운 게 아니라 그런 거짓말이 어렵다고요.
examples.trans: No, it is not that pink is difficult—telling that kind of lie is difficult.
Here the word for 'lie' is key.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.

examples.trans: So how is it?
So I went.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.

meanings.en: words, remarks (humble when referring to one's own speech to a superior)

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used as noun + locative (밑에).

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.

meanings.note: Means to air a program or, as in 방송하는 사람, to work in the broadcasting industry. RR: bangsonghada.

examples.trans: It broadcasts every evening.
People who work in broadcasting are busy.
What is your phone number?
Yes, that's right.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Used as bound noun + copula + -인데 (뿐인데).

examples.text: 그냥 핸드폰 꺼놓고 인터넷 하루 안 했을 뿐인데 그것만으로도 되게 좋더라고요, 시간도 많이 생기고.
examples.trans: All I did was switch off my phone and stay off the internet for one day, yet that alone felt wonderful and freed up so much time.
This point about merely, yet is really important.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
Did you hear about this relationship?
I was busy today because of relationship.

meanings.note: Used as passive prospective adnominal (생각될).

examples.text: 신디 씨가 연기를 워낙에 잘하셔서 모르는 사람이 본다면 정말 친한 사이가 아닐까 생각될 정도였습니다.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 아무래도 미래의 의사다 보니까 공부할 것도 많고.
examples.trans: Well, since I am a future doctor, I have a ton of studying to do.
Here the word for 'after all, naturally' is key.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (아무리).

examples.text: 아무리 생각해도 여기 오지 않았으면 좋았을 것 같아요. 우리 집 춘천이었는데 그날 내 생일이라고 졸라서 여기 온 거고.
